title: A good decay fit can still describe recording gain
question: Which model failures can residuals and window changes detect, and which remain exactly ambiguous?
model: Base=.2 exp(-4t)cos(2pi500t); overlap adds .06exp(-1.5t)cos(2pi512t); gain-drift multiplies base by exp(2t); alternate physical decay is .2exp(-2t)cos(2pi500t)
limits: Generated WAV bytes are not recorded physical data
Residual/window checks can reject some failures but cannot certify intrinsic damping
Exact exponential gain is a counterexample, not a claimed universal AGC law
Multiple modal contributions, support and microphone dynamics remain physical alternatives
incomingEvidence: S2A gained amplitude/phase robustness only under a single-mode, fixed-gain model. S1B already showed shared-chain assumptions can fail.
